    Is Howard an Ivy League school?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    No, Howard University is not an Ivy League school
    . It is, however, a top-ranked private HBCU (Historically Black College and University) frequently recognized as a leading member of the "Black Ivy League". It is often referred to as "the Mecca" or "Black Harvard" due to its prestige, influence, and academic standing. 
    Key Details About Howard University: 
    • The "Black Ivy League": Howard is included in the "Black Ivy League" (or "Black Ivies"), an informal group of top-tier HBCUs, which also includes institutions like Spelman College, Morehouse College, and Hampton University.
    • Ranking & Prestige: It is consistently ranked as one of the top HBCUs in the nation (often second only to Spelman) and ranks among national universities for its strong programs in law, medicine, and engineering

      Description

      Howard University is a private, historically black, federally chartered research university in Washington, D.C., United States. It is classified among "R1: Doctoral Universities – Very high research activity" and accredited by the Middle States Commission on Higher Education. It is the only HBCU with R1 designation. Wikipedia
      Address: 2400 6th St NW, Washington, DC 20059
      Acceptance rate: 41.3% (2024) IPEDS
      Undergraduate tuition and fees: 33,344 USD (2023 – 24) IPEDS
      Founded: March 2, 1867
      Mascot: Bison
      Phone: (202) 806-6100
